title: Phase 14 — Agent Engineering Checkpoint
description: Optional checkpoint on agent loops, tool use, and human-in-the-loop control.

questions.prompt: The canonical agent loop is best described as:
options: Prompt → answer, one shot
Reason → act (tool call) → observe → repeat until done
Ingest → embed → retrieve
Train → evaluate → deploy
questions.explanation: Agentic systems interleave reasoning, tool calls, and observation of results until the task completes or a budget/termination rule fires.

questions.prompt: An agent that gates irreversible actions behind explicit human approval should never be able to approve its own risky action.
questions.explanation: Self-approval defeats the purpose of the gate; approval records must come from a separate principal (the human) and be immutable.

questions.prompt: The main benefit of separating planning (ReWOO-style) from tool execution is:
options: Lower latency because the LLM decides the whole plan once before executing
More tool calls overall
Removes the need for tool schemas
Guarantees the task succeeds
questions.explanation: Planning up front avoids re-invoking the LLM between every tool call, cutting latency and cost cost; it doesn't remove schemas or guarantee success.

questions.prompt: Which best describes durable agent memory in a resumable system?
options: Prompt string held in RAM only
Persisted state (journal of steps, decisions, results) that survives process restarts
A long embedding cache
Retry counters
questions.explanation: Resumability requires persisted, ordered state that a restarted process can replay; RAM-only state dies with the process.

questions.prompt: Order the lifecycle of a gated tool action:
options: Agent classifies the action as risky (tier ≥ 2)
Agent requests approval and pauses in a persisted state
Human approves with an immutable record
Executor runs the action and records the result in the trace
questions.explanation: Classify, pause, get immutable approval, execute with trace. Skipping any stage breaks the audit chain.

questions.prompt: Select every honest way to evaluate an agent system:
options: Fixed task set with pass criteria written before running
Replaying recorded traces against the criteria
Judging by how impressive a single demo looks
Reporting failures and budget overruns alongside success rates
questions.explanation: Pre-registered criteria, replayable traces, and honest failure reporting define credible agent evaluation; curated demos do not.

questions.prompt: Describe what a Reflexion-style self-critique adds to an agent loop and when it can hurt.

criteria: Mentions loops/risk of reinforcing wrong hypothesis without new information

questions.explanation: Reflexion adds a verbal self-critique after failure and retries with the revised reasoning — useful when the failure was reasoning-shaped. It costs extra tokens and can circle forever if the real problem is missing information (no new tool results), so loop detection/budgets remain necessary.
